title: A MAGA County’s Top Election Official Wants to Hire Election Denial Superstar Tina Peters
gist: Shasta County, California's censured top election official, Clint Curtis, is trying to hire convicted election-fraud figure Tina Peters as a consultant to bypass hiring oversight, amid documented staff-abuse findings and skepticism from election-law experts that the appointment can actually proceed.

insights.claim: Shasta County's election registrar Clint Curtis is attempting to hire convicted election-fraud figure Tina Peters specifically as a 'consultant' rather than a formal employee, a structure he told local media is intended to bypass anticipated county efforts to block the appointment.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Illustrates a specific procedural workaround local officials can use to install controversial personnel outside normal hiring oversight, relevant to assessing governance risk in local election administration ahead of the midterms.
insights.locator: Curtis told the Redding Record Searchlight that he would be hiring Peters as a consultant

insights.claim: The county's deputy CEO states that no formal hiring process or application has actually been submitted for the position, and that any consultant contract would need to follow standard Shasta County policy, which has not been initiated, casting doubt on the practical viability of the announced hire.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Suggests the announcement may carry more political/media signaling value than near-term operational effect on the county's election apparatus.
insights.quote: There has been no formal process or application submitted to replace the current assistant registrar of voters
insights.locator: Buettell said that if Peters was hired as a consultant

insights.claim: A former Justice Department lawyer and head of the Center for Election Innovation and Research characterizes the hiring announcement as 'performance art' by an outgoing, censured official rejected by voters in the primary, arguing it is highly questionable that county funds or authority could legally be extended to a convicted felon.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: An expert read that existing legal and procedural mechanisms are likely to block the hire in practice, tempering the apparent severity of the controversy.
insights.quote: This announcement seems to be nothing more than performance art by the current and outgoing clerk, who was rejected by voters in the primary
insights.locator: some election experts believe mechanisms are in place

insights.claim: Colorado Governor Jared Polis commuted Tina Peters' state prison sentence in May 2026 after months of pressure from President Trump, and recently released court papers reportedly show Trump and his advisers coordinated with federal agencies to cut federal funding and grants to Colorado as part of that pressure campaign.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: A documented instance of using federal funding as political leverage tied to a single individual's clemency, relevant to tracking politicization of federal grant administration.
insights.locator: Colorado governor Jared Polis commuted Peters’ sentence in May

themes.theme: Institutional dysfunction at the county level

insights.claim: Clint Curtis, who had no prior election-administration experience and was living in Florida at the time, was appointed Shasta County's registrar in 2025 partly on the strength of touted associations with prominent election-denial figures including Mike Lindell, Mike Flynn, and Steve Bannon.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Illustrates a case where ideological network credentials substituted for domain experience in a consequential local election-administration appointment.
insights.locator: During the 2025 interview process for his current role

insights.claim: Curtis lost his June 2026 reelection bid to a career elections staffer with 18 years of experience and was subsequently censured 3-1 by the county Board of Supervisors following internal and external investigations that found he had threatened, verbally abused, and retaliated against his own staff, yet he retains hiring authority until his term ends.
insights.speaker: David Gilbert
insights.so_what: Highlights a governance gap where a lame-duck, censured official retains consequential staffing power, a structural risk for election-administration continuity ahead of the midterms.
